findings.description: PROTECTION CLAUSE ENTIRELY UNIMPLEMENTED (strongest). The spec's second conjunct is explicit: the system "shall protect the cell against manual edits ... so the live post-tax formulas ... evaluate numerically rather than against text or an operator-overwritten value." The real code contains nothing that protects anything: no AddProtectedRange / ProtectedRange / warningOnly / editors / DeleteProtectedRange, and — structurally decisive — the `SheetsViewClient` trait (lib.rs:426-465) exposes only `batch_update_view`, `set_tab_order`, `read_price_pass`, `write_stale_banner`, so there is no seam through which protection could even be requested. tests/formula.rs never asserts protection in any form. All 3 A runs emitted protection as a first-class, co-equal request (A1/A2/A3: `AddProtectedRange` with `warning_only: false` and a service-account-only editors allowlist, issued in the same batchUpdate as the value write so the cell is never numeric-but-unprotected). Real failure: an operator types `n/a` (or `20 %`, or a stray `=`) into H3; `=G3*H3` and `=G3*(1-H3)` then yield 0 or #VALUE!, which is exactly the outcome the requirement names, and nothing in the crate detects, reasserts, or overwrites it — the next republish rewrites the data range but the manual edit's format/protection state is unmanaged.

UNDOCUMENTED DEGRADED-RATE ENCODING: the empty string. lib.rs:585 writes `Cell::Value(eff_rate.map(fmt_ppm).unwrap_or_default())` — when the symbol is absent from `effective_rates`, H is written as `""`, not a percent-typed value, with no error and no marker. All 3 B runs reconstructed this as a first-class requirement (B1-d, B2-004, B3-4) including the downstream consequence: Sheets coerces empty to 0, so `=G*H` -> 0.00 and `=G*(1-H)` -> the full pre-tax G. The spec text says nothing about a missing rate at all, and this path directly contradicts its own words — `""` is not "a percent-typed userEnteredValue." Failure scenario: a position whose tax estimate degraded silently displays `Est. Unrealized Tax = 0.00` and `Net Unrealized = Unrealized P&L`, visually identical to a genuine 0% rate; the user reads an unhedged pre-tax number as a post-tax one. tests/formula.rs:164-168 tacitly concedes the case by searching for a populated row (`.find(|r| !r[rate_idx].text().is_empty())`) yet never asserts anything about the empty case.

EXACT PERCENT ENCODING PINNED BY CODE, LEFT OPEN BY SPEC. `fmt_ppm` (lib.rs:497-505) pins a precise literal grammar: optional leading `-` for negative Ppm, then `|ppm| / 10_000` as the whole part, `.`, then `|ppm| % 10_000` zero-padded to EXACTLY 4 fractional digits, then `%` — never trimmed, no thousands separator (Ppm(150_000) -> "15.0000%", Ppm(200_000) -> "20.0000%"). All 3 B runs reproduced this rule with the identical constants and the identical 4-digit padding. The spec offers only "e.g. a `\"%\"`-suffixed value" — it fixes neither precision, nor sign handling, nor separator policy. Related code-side surplus in the same area: the code emits NO number format at all — there is no `userEnteredFormat.numberFormat` / PERCENT request anywhere, so the cell's numeric typing rests entirely on Sheets' USER_ENTERED parse of the literal text (all 3 A runs emitted an explicit PERCENT numberFormat with a `0.00%` pattern alongside the value). Failure scenario: a workbook locale where `.` is not the decimal separator parses "20.0000%" as text or as 200000%, and nothing in the crate constrains it.

COLUMN GEOMETRY AND ROW-ANCHORING ARE LOAD-BEARING CONSTANTS THE SPEC NEVER STATES. `POSITIONS_HEADER` (lib.rs:174-188) fixes `Est. Tax Rate` at zero-based index 7 (column H) between `Unrealized P&L` at 6 (G) and `Est. Unrealized Tax (est)` at 8 (I); `render_positions` then emits the literal strings `=G{r}*H{r}` (lib.rs:568) and `=G{r}*(1-H{r})` (lib.rs:569) with `r = rows.len() + DATA_START_ROW`, `DATA_START_ROW = 2` (lib.rs:148, beneath the frozen header at row 1), each row referencing only its own row. All 3 B runs pinned all of it — index 7/H, the two exact formula shapes, DATA_START_ROW = 2, and the no-cross-row-leak rule (which tests/formula.rs:93-105 actively enforces). The spec names the consuming columns only by label (`Est. Unrealized Tax` / `Net Unrealized`) and states no letters, no anchoring convention, and no header/data-start split. Failure scenario: inserting a column before H (a pure header edit) silently repoints `=G*H` at `Unrealized P&L` × the wrong column while every test that keys columns by NAME (`col(name)`) still passes.

NOTHING ANYWHERE BOUNDS THE RATE'S DOMAIN — surfaced from both sides. The spec bounds nothing. The code bounds nothing: `fmt_ppm` explicitly formats negative Ppm with a `-` sign (lib.rs:500-503) and imposes no ceiling, and `render_positions` copies whatever `tax` supplied. The ONLY bound in the entire artifact is a test assertion against sample data — tests/formula.rs:184-187, `fraction.is_finite() && (0.0..=1.0).contains(&fraction)` — which all 3 B runs promoted to a stated invariant (B1-g, B2-007, B3-7) it is not. From the other direction, all 3 A runs independently invented a hard guard (`0..=10_000` bps, out-of-range => `Err(OutOfRange)`, explicitly "no clamping" because a silently clamped rate produces wrong Net Unrealized). Both directions are circling the same hole the requirement's own promise depends on. Failure scenario: an effective rate of Ppm(1_100_000) renders "110.0000%"; `=G*(1-H)` yields a NEGATIVE Net Unrealized on a profitable position and `=G*H` exceeds the entire unrealized gain, with no code path, no assertion, and no spec clause rejecting it. (Listed as BD, not as an A-only invention, because the [0,1] bound has real test-side presence, not merely A-side imagination.)

THE 'PARSES AS A NUMBER' GUARANTEE IS PROSE, NOT A PINNED BEHAVIOR. The spec makes the numeric-percent typing the operative requirement ("write the ... cell so Sheets parses it as a number (a percent-typed `userEnteredValue`)"). In the real artifact this exists ONLY as a doc comment on the trait method — lib.rs:439-446, "A `Cell::Value` is written as a Sheets `userEnteredValue` (NOT a forced string/`stringValue`) ... it MUST coerce to a number, never inert text" — delegated to an unwritten `runtime` implementor. No code in this crate sets a ValueInputOption or a userEnteredValue field, and no test asserts it: `est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply` (tests/formula.rs:146-202) only re-parses the Rust string, divides by 100 in Rust, and checks the algebra `G*h + G*(1-h) == G` — it would pass byte-identically if the real client wrote the cell as a forced stringValue, i.e. under the exact failure the spec forbids. All 3 A runs made this executable: an explicit `RepeatCell`/`UpdateCells` request with `fields: "userEnteredValue,userEnteredFormat.numberFormat"`. Interpretation note: A1/A2 read "percent-typed" as numberValue(0.20)+PERCENT format, A3 as the `"%"`-suffixed literal; the real code takes A3's reading but WITHOUT the accompanying numberFormat, which is the weakest of the three variants.

PROVENANCE AND KEYING PINNED BY CODE, ABSENT FROM SPEC. The rate is `tax`'s per-position `effective_rate_ppm` looked up by `Symbol` from a `BTreeMap<Symbol, Ppm>` (lib.rs:522-524, 561), written as `Cell::Value` and never `Cell::Formula` (asserted at tests/formula.rs:51-64 and :142), with `sheets-view` performing no rate arithmetic. All 3 B runs stated this as an explicit requirement (B1-b, B2-002, B3-2). The spec text names no source, no key, and does not say the cell must be a value rather than a formula — a live `=`-formula rate would arguably satisfy its literal words while breaking the crate's value/formula boundary and the settle-pass read-back model.

notes: Both directions carry material, largely non-overlapping surplus, plus one genuinely shared gap (rate domain), so BD-DRIFT rather than a single-sided classification. The headline is A-side and unambiguous: the requirement is a conjunction (percent-typed value AND edit protection) and the second conjunct has zero footprint in code, tests, or even the trait's method surface. Corroborating evidence from the other direction: 0 of 3 B runs mention protection, protected ranges, or manual-edit resistance in any form — the code gives a reconstructor nothing to infer it from, which is exactly what a missing conjunct looks like. A-side assumption artifacts EXCLUDED from findings per the direction rules (unanimous across A runs but with no basis in the spec text): carrying the rate as integer basis points `RateBps` mirroring Cents; deleting prior protected ranges for idempotency; the `0.00%` display pattern; single-batchUpdate atomicity of value+format+lock; caller-supplied GridRange for cell location. The one A-side split worth recording is interpretive, not structural: A1/A2 chose numberValue(fraction)+PERCENT format and explicitly argued a `"%"`-suffixed STRING risks the very text-coercion the spec forbids, while A3 took the spec's `e.g.` literally and wrote the `"%"` string plus a PERCENT numberFormat; the real code lands on A3's literal minus the numberFormat, i.e. the least-defended of the three readings, which is why finding 6 is graded as real drift rather than a taste difference. B-side runs are near-textually identical on every constant (index 7/H, 10_000 divisor, 4-digit zero-pad, DATA_START_ROW=2, `=G*H` / `=G*(1-H)`), so their surplus is high-confidence. B2/B3 additionally reconstructed "the Tax tab carries no formulas at all" — true of the code but out of this spec's scope, a whole-file read-through artifact, so it is not reported as a finding.
